gaps.sentence: She carried a suitcase in ___ hand.
gaps.explanation: 'Each hand' views the two hands individually; 'every hand' is not used for body parts this way.

gaps.sentence: He has lived in Berlin and Prague, and loves ___ cities.
gaps.explanation: 'Both cities' refers to the two cities mentioned; 'all' would suggest three or more.

gaps.sentence: Three out of four respondents — that is, the ___ — supported the change.
gaps.hint: three out of four = more than half
gaps.explanation: Three out of four is more than half, so 'the majority' is the correct label.

gaps.sentence: ___ of work has been done on the house since we bought it.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of work' fits the pattern '___ of work'; 'much of work' would need 'the', and 'few' is for countables.

gaps.sentence: This suitcase is ___ heavy to carry.
gaps.hint: adjective + this word + to-infinitive = impossible result
gaps.explanation: 'Too heavy to carry' means it is more heavy than possible; 'very' and 'so' cannot be followed directly by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: There is so ___ crime in this area that people are afraid.
gaps.explanation: 'So much' is used with uncountable nouns like crime; 'plenty' would need 'of'.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ point in complaining — no one will listen.
gaps.hint: fixed expression: ___ point in doing something
gaps.explanation: 'There's little point in doing something' means it is hardly worth doing; 'point' is uncountable here.
'Too cold to swim' means the temperature prevents swimming; 'enough' would follow the adjective.
